latest_publication.article_format: Construction workflow guide with six-gate CIS onboarding control map
latest_publication.title: How to automate CIS subcontractor onboarding without losing control
latest_publication.target_client_type: UK construction SMEs and contractors that repeatedly onboard and pay subcontractors under the Construction Industry Scheme
latest_publication.industry_or_operating_context: Construction operations, CIS subcontractor onboarding, HMRC verification, finance hand-offs and monthly-return readiness
latest_publication.primary_buyer_problem: Subcontractor identity, CIS verification results and payment treatment are copied across email, spreadsheets and finance systems, creating repeated admin and weak evidence around who was verified and why a deduction rate applies.
latest_publication.primary_search_intent: Understand how to automate CIS subcontractor onboarding while keeping employment-status judgement, HMRC verification, deduction treatment and required records controlled.
latest_publication.trend_or_durable_demand: Durable and current operational demand. HMRC continues to require verification before paying new subcontractors, monthly reporting of subcontractor payments and retention of specified CIS payment and deduction records. HMRC's CIS manual was updated in June 2026 and its contractor/subcontractor guide was republished in July 2026.
latest_publication.evidence_source_and_date: GOV.UK CIS contractor verification, record-keeping and monthly-return guidance checked 19 August 2026; HMRC Construction Industry Scheme manual updated 4 June 2026; CIS 340 guide published July 2026.
latest_publication.existing_article_gap: The site covers general client onboarding, invoice approval, purchase orders and system hand-offs, but not construction-specific CIS verification, subcontractor deduction treatment, record retention or monthly-return readiness.

comparison_against_previous_12.why_meaningfully_distinct: This article is a construction-specific CIS control workflow. Its core decision points are employment status, HMRC verification, deduction treatment, CIS record retention and monthly-return readiness. Existing onboarding and finance pages do not answer those questions.

latest_publication.original_editorial_asset: A six-gate CIS subcontractor onboarding control map covering status, identity, history, verification, payment setup and return readiness, with explicit stop conditions at each gate.
latest_publication.first_hand_contribution_or_limits: Uses Henry Oliver's business-analysis, data-control and automation perspective. It does not claim construction tax-advisory experience, make employment-status decisions or replace HMRC guidance.
latest_publication.proof_points_used_recently: The 200,000-SKU and eight-hours-to-two-minutes proof points were not reused in the article body.

latest_publication.readability_check: Passed editorial review for short sentences, active voice, plain British English and intended Hemingway grade 9 or lower.
latest_publication.mobile_check: Passed conceptual checks at about 390px and 768px. Content width is fluid, headings wrap, CTA text can span lines and the six-gate control table uses an overflow-safe wrapper.
latest_publication.ai_mention_check: Passed. AI is not mentioned because deterministic validation, HMRC verification evidence and explicit stop rules are more appropriate for this workflow.
